title: Frame bytes changed, signatures kept -> SIG_INVALID

source.model: S-P1 Q3 companion A (signature unbound), degraded

scenario: Change common.content identically in both frames (so the common bytes still agree) and keep both signatures.
choices: Altering object type or canonicalization version instead is caught earlier by the codec (CV_UNKNOWN, TAG_*), so the payload is the field that exercises the signature check (S-P1 F4).
The strict counterpart of the S-P1 trace is the capstone C-C5 strict run; S-P1's strict mutant m_D_signature has no archived .out.
partial_overlap: L-108 / HY-N2 / AGG-g (valid signature over other bytes; the dual form)

needs: A real receipt; re-encode frames and a_sig (no signing).

subcases.title: L0 form: not re-stamped
subcases.construction: A-a; post-issue: common.content set to {TEST: 'altered after signing'} in both frame payloads, a_sig re-encoded with the original S_kms, S_gpg; no re-stamp (the L0 form)
subcases.T_derivation: T null: a_sig changed after stamping, so the receipt proof's digest no longer matches (row 11.2); U null with T (A10.1.1)

subcases.title: TEST form: the altered A_sig re-stamped
subcases.construction: TEST issue, adversarial; sign hook replaces both frames with the altered-content frames after signing, so the new A_sig is stamped
subcases.T_derivation: T = nTime(h*) of the fixture's own receipt proof and headers (a_sig and receipt_anchor as stamped; rows 11.1-11.4 pass); U = 7200 + max nTime(h*..h*+5) (A10.1.1)
